During their chat, Savannah remarked to Hargitay that “everything you’re touching is turning to gold right now, including Jalen Brunson and the Knicks,” referencing the team’s NBA finals win in June, ending a 53-year championship drought.
“That is all super surreal still, all of that, but I’m really thrilled,” Hargitay replied.
Savannah also joked that Hargitay should continue to reveal more tea and hopefully, the actor’s wishes will materialize.
“We’ll have to manifest a few more,” Savannah said. “Let’s cook up some more stuff.”

Hargitay has actually managed to bring up the Knicks and her friendship with Brunson on several occasions. While appearing on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle in June, Hargitay referred to Brunson as a “friend” and said he’s “my inspiration.”
“He is so singular and magnificent. He’s a magnificent human,” she said.
When guest co-host Savannah suggested that Brunson should attend Hargitay’s Broadway show, the actor said, “Oh, he told me he’s coming!”
The ‘SVU’ star also sat down with Hoda Kotb for a June episode of her “Making Space” podcast in June and applauded the athlete and his teammates for their performance in the NBA Finals.
“Here, the Knicks have had this profound effect on the city and provided hope, but also the ability to dig deep and all of the things that we learn (like) never give up,” she said.
The actor spoke fondly of Brunson and praised “what he’s done and what he’s taught us and children.”
“So he’s teaching you? Jalen Brunson is teaching you?” Kotb asked.
“Every day,” Hargitay replied.

title: Nicole Kidman Looks Back on Marriage to Tom Cruise and the 3 Words She Told People Who Criticized it
summary: Nicole Kidman is looking back on her 10-year marriage to Tom Cruise and what she said to critics who cautioned her against marrying young.
story: Nicole Kidman is looking back on her 10-year marriage to Tom Cruise and what she said to critics who cautioned her against marrying young.
Speaking to British Vogue for the magazine’s September 2026 issue, Nicole Kidman said the marriage “thrust” her into new levels of fame in her early 20s.

Kidman was 23 when she married Cruise, then 28, in a 1990 ceremony in Telluride, Colorado. The couple met while co-starring in the film “Days of Thunder,” which also came out in 1990. Within five years, they had adopted two children, Isabella and Connor. They co-starred in “Eyes Wide Shut” in 1999.
“Suddenly I was 22, 23 years old and I had this huge movie star husband. But it just seemed completely natural. We just fell madly in love and it was that simple,” she said.
The actor said she received some cautionary advice before the wedding, which she ignored.

“I remember people saying to me, ‘OK, well this is really going to affect your career.’ I’m like, ‘I don’t care. I’m in love. I want to be married,’” Kidman said. “And then I was his ‘wife’ and they were like, ‘See, we told you.’ I’m like, ‘So what? I wasn’t meant to marry the man I love? Of course I’ll throw my career away. I don’t care.’”

Kidman, 59, did not throw her career away in the slightest, going on to win an Academy Award, six Golden Globes, two Emmys, and a BAFTA. This year alone, she’s starring in the sequel to “Practical Magic” and the TV shows “Lioness,” “Scarpetta” and “Margot’s Got Money Troubles.”

Kidman and Cruise shared they were separating in 2001. Kidman went on to marry Keith Urban and have two daughters with him, Sunday Rose and Faith. Last year, Kidman and Urban shared they were splitting after 19 years together.

Kidman has spoken about her relationship with Cruise sparingly. During an interview with New York Magazine for their Women in Power series in 2018, Kidman said she married Cruise for both love and “protection.”

“I got married very young, but it definitely wasn’t power for me — it was protection. I married for love, but being married to an extremely powerful man kept me from being sexually harassed. I would work, but I was still very much cocooned. So when I came out of it at 32, 33, it’s almost like I had to grow up,” she said.

title: New ‘Ted Lasso’ Stars Share Why It’s the ‘Perfect Show’ To Talk Challenges In Women’s Sports
summary: Between its signature cozy moments and laugh-out-loud bits, Season 4 of hit comedy “Ted Lasso” tackles some profoundly honest issues around women in sports.
story: Between its signature cozy moments and laugh-out-loud bits, the newest season of hit comedy “Ted Lasso” tackles some profoundly honest issues around women in sports. And the series’ stars say the medium is ripe for it.

Episode 2, released Aug. 12, introduces viewers to the kooky, eclectic members of Richmond’s women’s soccer team, the Lady Greyhounds. Several of the Season 4 newcomers tell TODAY.com that the show’s foray into the trials and tribulations around building a successful squad exposes some weightier topics like the major inequities that the women are up against. And it does so without “ramming it down the old throat,” says actor Faye Marsay.
“It’s the perfect show to do it because it’s about the underdog,” Marsay, who plays Lizzie, a soccer player and mom who’s juggling both roles, says.

title: Rob Gronkowski Reveals He Played Matchmaker for Julian Edelman at Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce’s Wedding
summary: Rob Gronkowski did his best to help his old New England Patriots teammate Julian Edelman find a love connection at Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s wedding.
story: Rob Gronkowski did his best to help his old New England Patriots teammate Julian Edelman find a love connection at Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s wedding.
The legendary tight end and current Fox NFL analyst shared on TODAY Aug. 13 that he and girlfriend Camille Kostek took Edelman along to the wedding of the year in July.
The couple tried to facilitate a spark with the single ladies for the former Super Bowl MVP, who was scoping out the star-studded crowd of attendees at New York City’s Madison Square Garden.
“Julian Edelman was the third wheel, so we were kind of looking for some girls for him,” Gronkowski said. “He was going, ‘Who’s that? Is she single?’ I’m like, ‘Go for it, Julian.’
“Camille and I were trying to play matchmaker, but no luck,” he added. “But Julian doesn’t need any luck. He’s a beautiful looking kid.”
While Gronkowski, 37, couldn’t find a potential love interest for Edelman, 40, he did bring his trademark zeal to the dance floor.

“The dance floor energy was top notch, and the wedding was top notch as well,” he said. “You couldn’t have painted a better picture of how the whole wedding went down. There’s no doubt about that. Everyone was on the (dance) floor, there was DJs, there was magicians going.”
It was a mini Patriots reunion, as another one of his former teammates, legendary quarterback Tom Brady, was also in attendance.
Kelce made his first public comments about his wedding during a press conference on Aug. 12 at the Kansas City Chiefs’ training camp.
His reflections came more than a month after the Chiefs star tight end and the global music superstar wed on July 3 in front of a star-studded guest list estimated to include 1,100 attendees.
“It was a fun offseason man,” Kelce said. “The wedding was the best night of my life, and I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us.”

There have been scant details that have trickled out about the wedding, which isn’t surprising considering attendees were required to sign non-disclosure agreements. Sources told NBC News that the bride and groom, who both wore white, each wrote their own vows in a “secret garden”-themed wedding.

The family has also shared only brief comments on the nuptials. Jason Kelce, Travis Kelce’s brother, said in an interview he “probably cried more at this wedding than I cried at my own wedding, which probably is not acceptable.”

title: Crowd Confused as Lana Del Rey’s ‘National Anthem’ Is Played Instead of ‘The Star-Spangled Banner’
summary: Ahead of a high school football game, a DJ played “National Anthem” by Lana Del Rey instead of the “The Star-Spangled Banner.”
story: In Lana Del Rey we trust.

The crowd at Waipahu High School in Hawaii was left confused when instead of hearing “The Star-Spangled Banner” ahead of their football game, Lana Del Rey’s “National Anthem” was heard through the speakers.
In video shared on TikTok Aug. 7 by user akikokelsa, people in the stands are on their feet anticipating the national anthem. However, that is not what begins playing.
“What’s happening? This is Lana Del Rey,” the person recording the video says, laughing.
Whens someone nearby asks if this is the wrong song, they reply, “Yeah, the song is called ‘National Anthem.’”
After a few seconds, over the loudspeaker, someone is heard asking, “DJ, can we have the national anthem, please?”
The person recording the video continues laughing at the slight mishap, noting that technically the DJ is playing a song titled “National Anthem.”
The comments section was filled with Del Rey fans who praised the user for instantly recognizing the track. Others joked that the singer’s song was the only anthem they stood by.
“No the dj was right the first time,” one person commented, with another adding, “Genuinely the ONLY national anthem I’d proudly stand for.”
“i love how you immediately knew😭 a true fan,” someone wrote, with the user replying, “SINCE 2013 BABYYY.”
“That’s the NATIONAL ANTHEM, no mistakes,” another commented.
Waipahu High School principal Zachary Sheets shared in a statement with NBC News that the DJ “experienced technical difficulties playing the songs.”
“Thankfully, our stadium announcer improvised quickly and led our crowd with a cappella versions of the national anthem and Hawaiʻi Ponoʻī,” he said.

Aside from the unexpected beginning, it was an exciting night for the Waipahu Marauders, who had a 40–17 victory over the defending state champions Campbell Sabers to reclaim the Cane Knife after 22 years.

title: Maria Canals-Barrera Reflects on Selena Gomez’s ‘Beautiful’ Wedding: ‘We All Cried’
summary: Maria Canals-Barrera, who portrayed Selena Gomez’s mom on “Wizards of Waverly Place,” opened up about attending Gomez’s wedding and giving her advice as a kid.
story: Over 20 years ago, Maria Canals-Barrera comforted and shared her motherly advice with generations of Disney Channel viewers and stars, including Selena Gomez.

As Theresa Russo, Canals-Barrera gave words of wisdom to her “Wizards of Waverly Place” daughter Alex Russo, portrayed by Gomez. Her nurturing nature also extended beyond the screen to real life, Canals-Barrera tells TODAY.com.

“She asked me for relationship advice a couple of times during the show,” Canals-Barrera recalls. “And that was really honoring to me because I play her mom. I’m not her mom ... So when (Gomez) asked me a couple of times about marriage and stuff, that was really touching to me.”
The two entertained audiences as mother and daughter for four seasons between 2007 and 2012, a time Canals-Barrera tells TODAY.com she remembers fondly.
So when Canals-Barrera attended Gomez’s wedding to Benny Blanco, she couldn’t help but get emotional. The couple got married in September 2025.
Years later, Canals-Barrera says she didn’t need to give her former on-screen daughter any advice. “Now, at her wedding, I think she figured it out,” she says.

Canals-Barrera posted a video on her Instagram that showed a side-by-side of her with Gomez on “Wizards of Waverly Place” and then at her wedding. Canals-Barrera shares that it was a moving celebration.
“(The wedding) was so beautiful. The vows that they wrote for each other were just so incredible. I mean, we all cried,” she says. “It was really beautiful. So I’m very happy that she found love.”
“She deserves the best and so does he,” she adds. “I wish them the best.”
The two would reunite again in the “Wizards” spinoff, “Wizards Beyond Waverly Place.” Canals-Barrera reprised her role as the Russo matriarch for two episodes, including the Aug. 4 finale.
Reflecting on working with Gomez over the years, she called her “a born talent.”
“She was on set knowing her lines, completely emotionally prepared and a singer to boot,” she says.
Also returning to her role of Connie Torres in “Camp Rock 3,” Canals-Barrera is forever grateful and honored to be the TV mom for many.

“It’s very encouraging as an actor, as a mother in real life, that the mothering moments mean something to (fans),” she says. “Even when it’s not our own mother. It’s very touching to us. The nostalgia vibe that’s happening right now. I’m so grateful to be part of it.”

title: Travis Kelce Breaks Silence on Wedding With Taylor Swift: ‘The Best Night Of My Life’
summary: Travis Kelce, the groom himself, is the latest to break his silence on America’s Royal Wedding between him and “Miss Americana” Taylor Swift.
story: Travis Kelce, the groom himself, is the latest to break his silence on America’s Royal Wedding between him and “Miss Americana” Taylor Swift.

At an Aug. 12 press conference at the Kansas City Chiefs’ training camp practice, Kelce opened up about the family and friends who joined them. The comments come more than a month after the couple wed in front of a star-studded guest list that was estimated to include 1,100 attendees.
“It was a fun offseason man,” Kelce said. “The wedding was the best night of my life, and I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us.”

Kelce and Swift tied the knot on July 3 at New York City’s iconic Madison Square Garden. Leading up to the big night, camera crews and fans alike lingered between 31st and 33rd Street in Manhattan, hoping to catch even a glimpse of the lovers.
Part of the couple’s security strategy involved losing the paper trail. In addition to NDAs, invitees received their invites electronically, a source who was invited told NBC News.

Since the wedding, few details have emerged about the event of the year. Sources told NBC News that the bride and groom, who both wore white, each wrote their own vows. Sources also said that the theme of the wedding appeared to be a “secret garden”  — fit for the “Speak Now” singer, to whom Kelce proposed while surrounded by flowers.

Kelce is not the first of his family to reveal details from the inside. Sister-in-law Kylie Kelce opened up about the tears Jason Kelce, Travis Kelce’s brother, shed. She said that the show of emotion was probably “more at this wedding than I cried at my own wedding.”

Later during the press conference, Travis Kelce reflected on the significance of having his wedding at the Garden, where some of the biggest names in both sports and music have cemented their legacies.
“MSG, man,” Kelce said before calling out Swift for attending the Knicks Finals — one of the recent iconic events held at the venue — while he was unavailable.
“I always told myself I’d go for a playoff game when the Knicks were rocking, and my wife went when I was stuck in mini camp, so I didn’t get my opportunity to go then,” Kelce said.
Kelce added that it was “kind of cool to be able to live out my childhood dream of being in that venue, the mecca of all sports venues.”
Kelce thanked the venue staff for allowing them to use the space given their request for privacy.
“It was perfect... and the AC was cooking; that was the best part,” he said.
The 36-year-old athlete is looking ahead to the upcoming NFL season.
“It was a crazy night,” Kelce said earlier during the conference. “It was full of a lot of celebration, but it’s football, baby.”

The upcoming NFL season kicks off Aug. 13 with preseason play. The official regular season scheduled to begin Sept. 9 with a Sunday Night Football game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks, airing on NBC and Peacock.

title: McDonald’s New Happy Meal Combines Hello Kitty and Godzilla: See the Toys
summary: McDonald’s new Hello Kitty & Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal combines characters from the Sanrio universe with monsters from the “Godzilla” film franchise.
story: McDonald’s is saying hello to not one but two iconic pop culture figures with its latest Happy Meal.
The fast-food chain is launching a new Hello Kitty & Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal, which combines characters from the Sanrio universe with monsters from the iconic “Godzilla” film franchise.

Everyone knows the most important part of a Happy Meal is the toy, and McDonald’s has created eight exclusive collectible toys as part of the collab.

The chain teased its newest Happy Meal on Instagram Aug. 10 by sharing a short clip of Hello Kitty eyeing a Happy Meal in the ocean. But she didn’t look quite like herself and had what appeared to be a monster suit on, complete with a fierce head and tail.
McDonald’s captioned the post, “cute meets kaiju 08.18.”
On Aug. 12, the fast-food chain made things official by sharing a photo of the toys customers can look forward to when they open up their Hello Kitty & Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal.
McDonald’s captioned the post, “cosplaying right into our hearts. Hello Kitty and Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal out 8.18.”

title: Harry Jowsey’s Reality Show Ends in a Real Wedding. Here’s Who He Marries
summary: Who does Harry Jowsey marry in the finale of Let’s Marry Harry? What happens in the finale?
story: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “Let’s Marry Harry.”

Twenty engagement rings later, Netflix heartthrob Harry Jowsey started the “Let’s Marry Harry” finale with two fiancés left and one difficult decision to make. And for much of the episode, it wasn’t clear he would make one at all.

The end of Episode 7 saw the “Too Hot to Handle” and “Perfect Match” star alone and emotional on the beach after visiting his family in New Zealand with his two finalists, Dannelle Davidson and Amber Mozo.
Sam Kruse, who rounded out Harry’s final three, made a sudden exit from the show at the start of Episode 7 after a series of conversations with Harry didn’t go to plan.

Despite only being a couple of days out from the altar, Harry started Episode 8, the finale, with no clarity about which of the two women he would say “I do” to. And to his close friends and members of his trusty support (and selection) squad, Sonny Henty and Amanda Kloots, he suggested a new option: abandoning both women altogether.

But ultimately, Harry did make a choice between Dannelle, 33-year-old cocktail waitress from Las Vegas, and Amber, 30-year-old travel photographer from Hawaii — one that brought all three of them to tears.
Read on to learn who Harry chose to spend forever with.
Who Does Harry Jowsey Marry in the ‘Let’s Marry Harry’ Finale?
With Dannelle all made up in her wedding glam and gown, Harry knocked on the door and sat down with her for a conversation.
Although he told Dannelle he’d fallen in love with her, he also said that he had “started second guessing everything,” and that the two were not going to get married.

“I don’t think you deserve someone that will second guess you, the person should know 100% and shouldn’t be worried about everything,” he told Dannelle. “I know that you deserve that at the bare minimum.”
“I thought it was something else this whole time with us but apparently it wasn’t,” she responded, in part. “I just feel stupid.”
After saying goodbye to one bride, Harry geared up to wait at the end of the aisle for his other one: Amber.

The Australian heartthrob became emotional immediately upon seeing Amber in her white dress, and the tears kept flowing throughout the ceremony as they gushed about their love throughout their vows — Harry’s pre-written and Amber’s spontaneous.

“You’re a miracle, and I know our dads are probably best friends up there,” Harry told Amber as he wore a pair of his dad’s glasses, whose memory he honored throughout the season. “You’re not just someone I fell for, you’re someone who makes me grow and look at life different.”
“I’m wearing these glasses because I want my dad to see how beautiful you are,” he added.
“Ending up here with you in this way is the best thing that’s ever happened to me,” Amber told Harry.
After they tied the knot, the night carried on with a celebratory reception packed with the bride and groom’s friends and family.
In a subsequent flashback sequence captured two weeks after the wedding, the newlyweds looked as in love as ever, enjoying beach days and time in bed.
Are Harry Jowsey and Amber Mozo Still Together Now?

Speculation about the couple’s current status has unfolded online since Amber posted an Instagram story in July on the shoulders of a man who doesn’t look like Harry. Neither Harry or Amber has publicly addressed their current relationship status.
The “Let’s Marry Harry” reunion is set to premiere Aug. 26.

title: ‘No Influencers’ Sign At Nantucket Craft Shop Sparks Massive Internet Debate
summary: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.

Nantucket has always been one of the most picturesque vacation spots in Massachusetts. But one small business on the island has sparked controversy for seemingly drawing a line in the sand, discouraging one particular group of tourists from visiting.

Four Winds Craft Guild, a store that sells handmade arts and crafts, recently installed a sign that reads “No Influencers,” inspiring a heated debate when they shared a photo of the sign on Instagram. Fans of the sign say it’s a cheeky reaction to the rise of influencer culture, while critics say it’s dismissive of social media content creators, many of whom are women.
John Sylvia, the owner of the store, told The New York Times that the sign was meant to be “tongue-in-cheek” and a reference to the rising popularity of influencer culture.
“I feel sometimes my store is used as someone’s background, a stage,” he said.
When Sylvia’s partner, Jessica Jenkins, initially shared a photo of the sign on Instagram, many influencers had strong feelings about the post. The social media platform later removed it.
How are fans and critics of the sign reacting? NBC’s Kaylee Hartung explored the brewing controversy in a segment for TODAY. Here’s everything you need to know.
Why Did the Shop Put Up a ‘No Influencers’ Sign?
In an interview with The New York Times, Sylvia said the sign wasn’t intended to be an attack on influencers.
“I don’t have this hatred toward influencers,” he said. “It was more of a joke. It is a problem we should look at as a society.”
The shop owner went on to say that many visitors come into the store to take photos and videos for social media and don’t speak to him or make purchases.
After Instagram removed the shop’s post, Jenkins shared a second post on July 27 with the following cheeky caption: “TAKE TWO 🎬.”

While speaking with The New York Times, Jenkins, a year-round resident on the island, described how influencers have impacted the culture on Nantucket. For starters, she said she notices an influx of “people creating videos on corners of themselves sipping an iced coffee and looking over their shoulder and doing a shoe kick or whatever.”
“I feel that whenever I open Instagram, I see someone show me a guide of what to wear, a guide of where to eat, a guide of what to buy, a guide of how to pack for Nantucket,” she said.

Nantucket has faced increased tourism over the years, with long lines at businesses. Former “Real Housewives of New York City” star and influencer Bethenny Frankel said in a social media video Aug. 1 the island has become an “absolute zoo.”
According to Nantucket’s government website, the island has a year-round population of around 11,000 but peaks in July and August to more than 50,000.
Why Is the ‘No Influencers’ Sign So Controversial?
The shop’s post instantly drew criticism from many influencers.
“How stupid can you be to put a sign in a store that prohibits basically free marketing?” TikTok user @kristinacanale asked in a recent video.
TikTok user @ivyynielsen shared a similar sentiment, saying, “It sent the message that creators aren’t welcome, and I don’t think that’s fair.”
Instagram user @levicoralynn offered the following take in a video, saying, “I think hating influencers has become a socially acceptable way to hate women.”
Though Four Winds Craft Guild made no mention of women in its sign, women make up a large percentage of lifestyle influencers, leading some critics to interpret the sign as an attack on women.
Lifestyle creator Paige Lorenze, who opened a boutique in Nantucket earlier this summer, commented on the original Instagram post, saying the sign was an attempt to “delegitimize” and “mock” women.
“It’s just a strange message coming from a store that celebrates a craft with such a rich history of women shaping the island and its economy,” she wrote.
But despite the backlash, some social media users saw the humor in the sign.
“This sign is funny!” Instagram user @lawyerlimor said in a video. “It’s funny!”
TikTok user @thedanahaffner shared the following reaction: “What happened to humor?? It’s just a little bit of like local humor.”
TikTok user @tiesyn supported the shop owner in a video, saying, “Don’t come in here acting entitled. More stores need to have a sign like that.”
Others Areas Have Attempted to Restrict Influencers
The rise of influencer tourism has led some vacation destinations to place restrictions on visitors in recent years.
In 2023, neighbors living near Sleepy Hollow Farm in Vermont created a petition to close nearby roads and prevent influencers from inundating the streets to snap photos of fall foliage.
One island in Finland also declared itself phone-free and started giving tourists stickers to cover their screens in an effort to help them enjoy nature.

Portofino on the Italian Riviera established “no-waiting zones” in 2023, with potential fines up to €275 to curb what the town’s mayor called “anarchic chaos” — tourists stopping to take selfies, per the BBC.

title: After Landing ‘Rockford Files’ Reboot Role, David Boreanaz Asked James Garner’s Daughter for Her Blessing
summary: David Boreanaz shared what he told James Garner’s daughter, Gigi Garner, after he was cast to lead NBC’s reboot of “The Rockford Files.”
story: When David Boreanaz learned he would lead NBC’s reboot of “The Rockford Files,” he knew he had to reach out to James Garner’s daughter, Gigi Garner, to receive her “blessing.”

The 57-year-old actor has been a constant on network television for decades, with starring roles on “Buffy the Vampire Slayer,” “Angel,” “Bones” and “SEAL Team.” But soon he will take on a new challenge as he inherits James Garner’s iconic role of Jim Rockford, a Los Angeles private investigator who relies on unconventional means to solve his crimes. James Garner, who died on July 19, 2014 at the age of 86, played the character on the original NBC series for six seasons from 1974 to 1980.

At NBC’s Backlot Pass 2026 event on Aug. 10 previewing the network and Peacock’s fall and midseason lineup, Boreanaz spoke about being inspired by the late actor, which made him want to contact Gigi Garner to assure her that her father’s legacy was in good hands.
During a panel conversation with “The Rockford Files” writer and executive producer Mike Daniels, Boreanaz explained how he got in touch with Gigi Garner to inform her of the casting news.

He said he has known the author and singer for over 15 years. He previously purchased a pinball machine from her that was a prop on her father’s show “Maverick.” But, the two had lost touch over the years. After landing the role, he found Gigi Garner’s old email address and decided to send her a message.
“I was like, I’m just going to give it a shot. I sent the email out and, to my surprise, she replied back. And I said, ‘I have to have a conversation with you,’” he recalled.
They chatted on the phone and he told her about the reboot.

“And she said, ‘Yeah, OK. I don’t know who’s going to play my father.’ And I said, ‘Well, they offered me the role,’” he continued. “And the first thing I said to her is, ‘A, I need your blessing. But first and foremost, I’m not going to play what your father did. What your father did is iconic and he’s already climbed that mountaintop. I inspire to do the same with this character, but I’m not imitating him.’”
In fact, Boreanaz told the panel audience that he didn’t grow up a fan of “The Rockford Files” and had never seen an episode.
He emphasized to Gigi Garner that he only had one goal: to make her dad proud.
“That’s it. Simple and clean and do the work,” he told her.
After they hung up, he said he went for a swim and thanked James Garner.

“I know that he’s with us. I know that he was with us in the pilot. I understand that’s a little too esoteric to think of, but that’s who I am as a person. I believe in that. I believe (the) universe has brought us to this specific moment and I do believe he’s with us,” he shared.

Another important figure in Boreanaz’s life who he has been thinking about as he enters the next chapter of his career is his mother. He said a “piece of him” owes the “Rockford” role to her because she pointed out the “uncanny” resemblance between him and James Garner years ago.
Boreanaz shared that when he was working on “Bones” his mother told him he needed to find a project connected to “The Great Escape” star.
“My mother’s spirit obviously brought that to light, somehow. So I thank my mom a little bit for that energy,” he added.
While executive producer Daniels also noted the similarities between Boreanaz and James Garner, he said the two share more characteristics that made him the perfect actor for the reboot.

“David obviously has a resemblance to Garner, but there are moments in this pilot and moments when we were on set shooting it that he would suddenly look in the camera and it was just uncanny,” Daniels said. “It wasn’t just the features. It was the half smile, the charm, the smirk, the twinkle behind the eye. It just suddenly all fit.”

He added, “Certainly, when we cast him, we were like, ‘Oh, great. He even kind of looks like the guy,’ you know. And then he got on set and we were like, ‘Whoa, he feels like the guy too in how he’s inhabiting this character.”

NBC announced it greenlit a contemporary reboot of “The Rockford Files” with Boreanaz in a press release in May. The show is expected to premiere in January 2027, with an exact date to be announced this fall. Joining Boreanaz will be Academy Award nominee Jacki Weaver, Michaela McManus and Felix Solis.

The logline for the series will sound familiar to fans of the original: “Newly paroled after doing time for a crime he didn’t commit, James Rockford returns to his life as a private investigator using his charm and wit to solve cases around Los Angeles. It doesn’t take long for his quest for legitimacy to land him squarely in the crosshairs of both local police and organized crime.”
However, Daniels clarified at the panel that the show will not be a “one‑for‑one, apples‑to‑apples remake.”

“I think you can kind of get in trouble with people who are sentimental with the original. It just becomes a comparison: who is the actor they remember loving as a kid and who’s the actor playing it now,” he explained.
Instead, he said he hopes to recapture the feeling fans experienced when they watched the classic.

title: Sugarland Is Taking Breakout Album ‘Enjoy the Ride’ Back on Tour for 20th Anniversary
summary: Sugarland is hitting the road for their “Ride Or Die Tour” for a very special reason: the 20th anniversary of their breakout album “Enjoy the Ride.”
story: Sugarland is hitting the road for a very special reason.
To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their hit album “Enjoy the Ride,” the country duo is heading out on tour this fall.

On Aug. 11, Jennifer Nettles and Kristian Bush sat down with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones to discuss their exciting announcement and give a preview of what fans can expect from the aptly named the “Ride Or Die Tour.”

Nettles and Bush will be touring cities across the country from Oct. 1 to Nov. 21 to celebrate the album that solidified their spot as country icons. The official Instagram account for the duo released the official lineup of dates Aug. 11. Ticket presale begins Aug. 12 at 10 a.m. followed by general onsale Aug. 14.

Following its 2006 release, “Enjoy the Ride” went triple platinum. Throughout their time as a band, Sugarland has sold nearly 10 million albums in the U.S. The duo has won two Grammy Awards,  five ACM Awards and five consecutive CMA Awards for vocal duo of the year, from 2007 to 2011.
Nettles specifically points to “Enjoy the Ride” as a “turning point” in their career.
“Our debut album was great, but then this (was) really like when people started to really catch on to what we were doing and like it,” she said.

Bush said the album holds a special place in Sugarland’s heart since it was the first one they produced together. Outside of the band, Bush himself has produced an endless amount of music for other artists.
“Dreaming up how things sound and how they feel, it’s something I’ve been doing my whole life,” he said.
Looking back on their band’s enduring success, Nettles said she has “so much gratitude,” and Bush echoed her sentiments.
After collaborating for several decades, Bush and Nettles have a simple secret for forming a successful working relationship that lasts.

“I think like any relationship, you keep it fresh and you communicate. It doesn’t matter if it’s family. It doesn’t matter if it’s intimate. It doesn’t matter if it’s creative. Whatever, like keep it fresh. We do obviously other things. Kristian’s a fantastic producer (and) has hit records out the wazoo with Megan Moroney right now,” Nettles said.
Bush added that he and Nettles are a “unique duo” for one particular reason.

“Almost every single time we’ve sat down to do anything, maybe even in the dressing room before we walked up here, we will come up with ideas on the spot that work almost every time. And I don’t know what that (is), you know, I grab onto her,” he said.

Before announcing their new tour, Sugarland teased some exciting news on their Instagram account, posting a video of the country duo taking a bow on stage. The band captioned the post, “It’s been a minute...” and added the words “Coming soon” to the end of the video.

The day before announcing their tour, Sugarland shared another video of Nettles and Bush performing. As a plethora of excited fan comments appeared in the video, the words “We hear you!” could be seen at the end of the short clip.
Sugarland added fuel to the fire, captioning the post, “Don’t miss out...”

Sugarland released their last album in 2018 with “Bigger,” reuniting after going on hiatus starting in 2012. Nettles and Bush last toured together as Sugarland in 2024, co-headlining the “Take Me Home Tour” with Little Big Town.

title: QVC’s Toni Brattin Says She ‘Froze’ After That Viral Mishap: ‘I Just Went Down!’
summary: Jimmy Fallon had a visit from QVC wig mogul Tami Brattin days after her viral moment.
story: Jimmy Fallon’s comedic take on a viral QVC on-air moment has viewers wigging out.
The host of “The Tonight Show” welcomed TV personality Toni Brattin to his show Aug. 10 and spoofed an embarrassing moment she experienced during a recent QVC segment.
In case you missed the hilarious moment, Brattin was showcasing her collection of wigs on air when she accidentally made a NSFW reference.
While describing the wig she was wearing, Brattin said, “It looks like you went and got a blowjob.” She quickly self-corrected, saying, “a blowout at your salon.”
Terri Conn, a QVC host who was also present for the segment, quickly intervened and reminded viewers that they could take advantage of a “huge beauty sale.”
As Conn began to speak, Brattin shook her head and lowered herself to the floor, out of the camera frame.

After viewing the awkward on-air moment, Fallon poked fun at it during an episode of “The Tonight Show” last week, saying, “Note to all the married men out there: The wig is only available on your birthday, apparently.”
When Brattin saw the clip, she applauded Fallon for his witty comment during an interview with TMZ.

“Jimmy, hat’s off. I had to laugh at him as much as I had to laugh at myself. I happened to save one of those wigs just for Jimmy and I would love to see what this wig would look like on Jimmy. So Jimmy, you just tell me when your birthday is and I’ll hand deliver this and we’ll see how cute you look in it,” she said.
Brattin kept her promise and appeared on “The Tonight Show” Aug. 10.
Fallon set the scene for the segment, saying, “My birthday is actually coming up.”
Brattin then appeared and waved a brown wig in the air.
“I think that you handled that perfectly, by the way. You really nailed it,” Fallon told Brattin of her viral moment.
The TV host then asked the QVC personality what she was thinking as she slowly sank out of the camera frame after her on-air flub.
“Well, you know, I was kind of froze(n) and I was trying to decide, ‘Do I go to the left? Do I go to the right?’ I just went down,” she said.
Brattin then showed Fallon the brown wig she selected for him and put it on his head.
“Oh, look at all that hair!” she said.
“Yeah, you love it?” Fallon replied.
“And how about the volume in the back?” she added.
“Oh yeah. I love it,” Fallon said, then posed. “I’m honored. I love it.”
Brattin paused to fluff up the wig a bit then covered her face and laughed as Fallon exclaimed, “I am blown away.”
The duo ended the segment by turning their backs to the camera and lowering their bodies as they introduced “The Tonight Show” house band, The Roots.

title: Iran rejects ‘delusions’ after Trump says he wants the Strait of Hormuz to be a U.S. territory
summary: Iran called on the U.S. to “accept the reality of defeat” after President Donald Trump said he would declare the Strait of Hormuz a “territory” of the U.S.
story: TEHRAN, Iran — A defiant Iran called on the U.S. to “accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in delusions” after President Donald Trump suggested that he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz a “territory of the United States.”

The crucial waterway that handled one-fifth of the world’s oil before the war “cannot be seized with a tweet, nor with an aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order, nor through an election speech,” Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a post on X early Saturday.

“This strait will only be opened and closed under Iran’s command, and as long as you do not accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in delusions, Iran will continue to enforce the blockade,” he added.

With oil tanker traffic through the strategic strait at a trickle and peace talks between the U.S. and Iran at an impasse, there are few signs that the war, launched on Feb. 28, is close to being over.

A 60-day negotiating period intended to hammer out a deal to end the conflict, set when Trump and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in mid-June, ends on Monday with few direct negotiations having taken place.

Speaking Friday at a police academy in Nassau County, New York, Trump said Iran was being “very badly defeated,” and once victory was secured, “pretty soon, I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.”

Urging Americans to accept slightly higher gasoline prices, he told the crowd of law enforcement officers that “a tiny little bit more” at the pump was worth the cost of ensuring “a very ⁠evil country” could not have a nuclear weapon, one of his stated reasons for the war.

Global oil and gas markets have calmed since prices spiked at the start of the war, but prices are still significantly higher than before the conflict, and rose again early Friday. Crude oil futures rose $1 a barrel on Friday while benchmark Brent futures were on track for a weekly rise of 6.0%, Reuters reported Saturday.
Which economy would benefit the most from end of U.S.-Iran war?

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains a trickle of the 130-140 vessels that typically traverse it during peacetime. Only two vessels passed through the strait on Friday, with no crude oil shipments visible, according to analysis from ship-tracking firm Kpler.
While some ships have turned their transponders off and risked crossing undetected, Iran continues to fire on ships attempting to transit despite the U.S. blockade of the Islamic Republic’s ports.

A ​bulk carrier was struck in the hull by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre ‌said on Saturday. The organization run by the British navy that helps protect commercial shipping in high-risk areas added that the crew was safe, although no damage assessment had ⁠been reported and the environmental impact was unknown.

Vice President JD Vance, who has been tasked with leading negotiations to end the war, told Fox News on Thursday that the No. 1 goal was to “keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country.” He added that “obviously goal No. 2 is ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon.” Tehran has repeatedly insisted it has no desire to develop one.

Trump and his team have offered various reasons for the conflict, initially saying they wanted to support mass antigovernment protests, before prioritizing a desire to end Iran’s nuclear program and topple the hard-line Islamic regime.
In an interview with Iran’s Shahrara News published Friday, the country’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said there were “no negotiations currently taking place between Tehran and Washington.”

Qatar and Pakistan, as mediators, were exchanging messages and remained in contact with Iran, “but this does not at all constitute negotiations,” he said. “No decision has yet been taken to resume talks with America.”

title: ‘Revenge is inevitable’: Iran ramps up propaganda war with violent billboards
summary: Anti-U.S. messaging has intensified in recent weeks following the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with artificial intelligence playing a major role.
story: The billboards are state-sponsored, plastered across Iran’s capital and far from subtle. One features an image of President Donald Trump lying in a casket; another shows the White House on fire; a third is a parody of the American flag with skulls in place of the stars and bombs dropping from the stripes.

Alongside ads for a multitude of products such as cars and shampoo, the giant billboards have become familiar sights to the people of Tehran in recent years. But since the country’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was killed in an airstrike on the first day of the war launched by the United States and Israel, the messaging has become bolder and the tone more violent during the almost six-month conflict.

title: In an apparent shift, Vance says lowering oil prices is ‘goal No. 1’ of Iran war
summary: Keeping gas prices low is now the United States’ “goal No.
story: Keeping gas prices low is now the United States’ “goal No. 1” in the Iran war, Vice President JD Vance has said, as Washington threatened an indefinite naval blockade and signaled it would soon intensify economic pressure on Tehran.
The comments appeared to be the latest shift in the public rationale for the conflict, with Vance ranking Iran’s nuclear ambitions second.

The vice president’s remarks came as the Trump administration embraced a long-term effort to inflict more damage on the Islamic Republic, despite growing signs of strain on American forces and domestic pressure ahead of the midterm elections.

President Donald Trump has suggested a shift away from military force in favor of “low-keying it” with economic pressure. That followed a deadly cycle of tit-for-tat exchanges that produced no clear resolution and depleted U.S. reserves of missile interceptors.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Oil and gas prices spiked worldwide after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28. Markets have since calmed since that early peak, but prices are still significantly higher than before the conflict and rose again early Friday after the most recent remarks from Vance and others.

“I know that oil is down today and it’s way down from the highs in the early days of the conflict,” Vance told Fox News on Thursday, before the latest uptick. “That’s goal No. 1 — keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country.”
He added that “obviously goal No. 2 is ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon.” Tehran insists it has no desire to develop one.

Trump and his team have offered various reasons for conflict with Iran, initially saying they wanted to support mass anti-government protests, before prioritizing a desire to defang Iran’s nuclear program and even topple the regime.

title: Jason Arday, ex-Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, found dead a week after resigning
summary: Former Cambridge professor Jason Arday was found dead at his London home on Friday, one week after he resigned from his position after accusations of plagiarism.
story: A former Cambridge professor was found dead at his London home on Friday, one week after he resigned from his position at the esteemed university following accusations of plagiarism.
Jason Arday, 41, became the youngest Black professor at Cambridge when he was hired as a professor of sociology of education in 2023.

London’s Metropolitan Police force said it responded to a report of a man found unresponsive inside a property on Friday and that the man was pronounced dead at the scene, without naming Arday. Authorities said the death is being treated as “unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious.”

“We are desperately saddened to hear this tragic news. Our heartfelt sympathies go to Jason Arday’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time,” University of Cambridge Vice-Chancellor Deborah Prentice said Friday.

Arday was known for his neurodivergence; he had said he was diagnosed with autism as a child and was unable to speak until the age of 11. He went on to forge a path in academia as a scholar of race, inequality and education.
Arday had resigned on Aug. 5 following scrutiny over alleged plagiarism in his academic work and questions about his accomplishments.

Last month, questions regarding his qualifications were raised publicly by Nathan Cofnas, a former Cambridge philosophy researcher who left the institution after critiquing diversity, equity and inclusion programs.

The Times of London had subsequently published an analysis of Arday’s 2015 Ph.D. thesis highlighting passages that it said were “identical or near-identical” to an earlier paper written by another researcher.
In the weeks since, British media outlets led intense and prolonged scrutiny of Arday’s work, also interrogating a history of claims about his childhood and personal life.

A statement from Arday’s family said he was “a gentle man and who always wanted to see the best in everyone,” condemning critics who they said “would leave no stone unturned in their quest to undermine him.”
Cambridge professor Simon Baron-Cohen, director of the university’s Autism Research Centre, told the BBC he was in touch with Arday hours before his death.

He said Arday “was being subjected to relentless scrutiny, including ridicule, discrediting absolutely every detail of his life,” adding that he “wasn’t coping with the loss of his career, the loss of his reputation, and he felt he couldn’t go on.”

Baron-Cohen said that Arday had believed “there was a racist playbook to discredit Black academics in universities, and that they used accusations of plagiarism to try and bring down Black academics,” adding that Arday referred to former Harvard President Claudine Gay, who resigned two years ago while facing plagiarism allegations and criticism over her comments on antisemitism.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday that the death was “a tragedy on so many levels,” adding that “it’s not a moment for any rushing to judgment. It’s a moment for reflection, I would say.”

Other figures were more vocal in questioning his treatment by the media. London Mayor Sadiq Khan said on X that Arday had faced “an unacceptable public hounding and campaign of abuse” and that he “was the victim of a pernicious public shaming that other people in his position simply wouldn’t have faced.”

Hacked Off, a campaign group that supports regulation of the media, called for an “inquiry into the culture and behaviour of the British press” following the death, saying scrutiny “went far beyond any limited public interest considerations around academic standards.”
While Cambridge initially defended Arday, on Aug. 5 it opened an investigation “following new information about Professor Arday’s qualifications and honorary appointments.”

In his resignation statement last week, Arday described his tenure as “the privilege of my life to teach my students,” but conceded “the years since my appointment have also been marked by an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack.”

“While criticism is an inevitable part of academic life, what I have experienced has gone far beyond scholarly disagreement. The relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love,” he continued.

In a statement Thursday, Cambridge’s Prentice shared an update on the inquiry into Arday, saying the university would investigate the circumstances around his appointment by the Faculty of Education in 2022 and his time at Cambridge.

She also said she asked the university council’s deputy chair and council’s audit committee to establish terms for an independent review of all university processes that will take place alongside the probe into Arday.
In his resignation announcement, Arday said he reached a point where the “personal cost becomes too great.”

“For my own wellbeing, for my family, and for those who have stood by me throughout this difficult period, I have concluded that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away,” he said.

Arday’s memoir, “Great and Unfortunate Things,” was released earlier this week in the U.S., giving an account of his childhood — from being diagnosed with autism and developmental delays at the age of 3 — to speaking by the age of 11 and reading and writing by the age of 18.

“Without romanticizing the struggle, this is a story of determination against seemingly insurmountable odds — and of a family and a small group of believers whose compassion helped him see what is possible,” a description for the book by publisher Simon & Schuster said.

title: Magnitude-7.7 quake hits off coast of Indonesia, killing at least 47
summary: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of Indonesia in the eastern Flores region, the United States Geological Survey reported on Friday.
story: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of Indonesia in the eastern Flores region, the United States Geological Survey reported on Friday.
The epicenter was 42 miles north-northwest of the city of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province.
At least 47 people have been killed, the ​National Disaster Management Agency said Saturday.
Rescue teams have yet to reach Nagekeo, the region ‌closest to the epicenter, after landslides blocked roads and disrupted communications, officials said.

“The quake was massive, the shock was so strong,” Nona, a 51-year-old resident of Talibura, a village in East Nusa Tenggara, told Reuters. “There were 13 of us inside the house and we all ran to save ourselves.”

Earlier, ​rescuers in the port town of Maumere found 20 dead, six injured and two trapped under the rubble, ⁠said Fathur Rahman, head of the city’s rescue agency. Maumere is the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in the east of ​Indonesia’s vast archipelago.
Residents remain trapped in several buildings in earthquake-affected areas, with reports of landslides blocking several roads.

Preliminary data ​showed 157 homes were heavily damaged, 41 moderately damaged and 148 lightly damaged. Damage was also reported at 87 schools, 18 health facilities, five places of worship and six office ‌buildings, along ⁠with other infrastructure.
The quake was felt across much of Flores Island, with reports indicating heavy damage.
Yohanna Embu, a resident of Sikka Regency, said a number of buildings were damaged by the strong shaking and panicked people ran to higher ground.
“Many buildings here were damaged. ... I saw that the waiting room at the port terminal in Maumere had collapsed,” she said.

Indonesian authorities initially issued a tsunami warning for parts of East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi provinces, and urged residents to stay away from beaches and riverbanks, and residents on the coastline to move to higher ground. The agency located the shallow undersea quake near Flores Island.
The initial quake was followed by two aftershocks.

Students at St. Peter Major Seminary in Sikka who were attending morning Mass fled in panic when the roof of an assembly hall collapsed, said the Rev. Guidelbertus Tanga, rector of the seminary, which is known locally as Ritapiret Seminary on the predominantly Catholic island of Flores.
“Our students and nuns ran out in panic beneath a collapsing roof,” Tanga said, “At least one priest suffered a broken leg after jumping from the second floor of a building during the quake.”
Separately, Australia’s tsunami warning center said the undersea earthquake will have “no tsunami threat to the Australian mainland, islands or territories.”

Indonesia, a vast archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, is prone to earthquakes and volcanic activity because of its location on the “Ring of Fire,” an arc of volcanoes and fault lines in the Pacific Basin.
In December 1992, a magnitude-7 earthquake caused a tsunami that killed about 2,500 people on the southeastern island of Flores, part of a group of islands in the eastern half of Indonesia.
The latest quake comes after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake rocked western Colombia on Monday, causing widespread damage.
In June, deadly back-to-back earthquakes, with magnitudes of 7.2 and 7.5, killed more than 6,000 people in Venezuela, according to government figures.

title: ‘Tinderbox’ Britain bans disposable barbecues, sends nationwide fire alerts as Europe battles blazes
summary: LONDON — The U.K. imposed a temporary ban on the sale of disposable barbecues and sent a nationwide alert warning of a “very high risk of wildfires” as European countries battle to keep blazes under control.
story: LONDON — The U.K. imposed a temporary ban on the sale of disposable barbecues and sent a nationwide alert warning of a “very high risk of wildfires” as European countries battle to keep blazes under control.

Authorities are bracing for the prospect of fires breaking out in the days ahead, with drought conditions across much of Britain and a prolonged heat wave this week bringing temperatures in excess of 38 degrees Celsius (100 degrees Fahrenheit).

“Britain is a tinderbox right now,” Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned on Friday as he visited the scene of a fire in Stourbridge, in the West Midlands region, that destroyed 19 homes. “I’ve never seen scenes like this in Britain,” he added.

Wildfires are not typically a major threat in Britain, usually known for a temperate maritime climate and frequent wet weather, even in the summertime. The U.K. does not have any firefighting planes, a common sight in many other countries, but Burnham said he would seek to commission some in an effort to “face up” to the “changing climate.”
“Farmers are watching crops fail and firefighters have faced hundreds of wildfires in a matter of weeks,” he added in a video shared on X. “This is what climate change looks like here and now.”
Many of England’s rolling green fields are currently a sea of brown, dried-out grass, with firefighters and officials fearing any spark could lead to catastrophe.
One Stourbridge resident said that trees were “exploding” in the conditions as the fire spread.
“We just grabbed everything and left,” Paul Nash, whose garden was damaged, told Reuters.
Burnham also announced a temporary ban on the sale of popular disposable barbecues.

“Retailers have been informed that disposable barbecues must be removed from sale immediately. The temporary measure will remain under review but will stay in place while the heightened wildfire risk continues,” the U.K. government said in a statement.

Emergency alerts were sent to phones across England and Wales nationwide on Friday, warning: “Residents, landowners and visitors should not undertake any activity that could start a fire, including disposable barbeques, firepits, garden incinerators or fireworks.
“Even a small flame can rapidly develop into a major wildfire placing lives, homes, businesses and emergency responders at risk,” the alert continued.
Phil Garrigan, chair of the National Fire Chiefs Council, said the number of wildfires seen this year had already surpassed all-time records.

“We’re only in the middle of August, and the wildfire season seems to extend way into November at this moment in time. So, we’re ⁠anticipating this being not just a record-breaking year, but a considerable increase on the number of wildfires previously experienced,” he told Reuters.
“We’ve declared 11 major incidents over the course of ⁠the last 24 hours,” Garrigan added.

“The demands and the requests for support have probably outstripped the capability of the U.K. fire and rescue service ... so we’ve struggled to ‌give fire and rescue services exactly ​what they want.”
Fires spread across Europe

Many European countries are battling fires after a long stretch of hot and dry conditions. A raging wildfire in the province of Huelva, southern Spain, triggered an operation to evacuate around ​700 people on Thursday.

More than 2,000 people evacuated ​the village of Gey in western Germany on Friday after a ‌wildfire near the Belgian border, while France evacuated 525 people from the village of Luglon in its southwestern Landes region.

Meanwhile, Croatia and Greece both evacuated tourists from resorts as fires spread. Flames enveloped settlements and trees around Omis, a scenic town on Croatia’s prized Dalmatian coast surrounded by trees and ⁠rocky hills, officials said, injuring 40 and forcing 1,200 to ​evacuate.
More than 300 people were evacuated by boat from Siviri in northern Greece, south of the country’s second city, Thessaloniki.

People wearing face masks, some clutching children or pets, boarded dinghies and boats in the seaside town as a wildfire ate through the nearby forest and columns of smoke turned the cloudless sky a dark gray.

title: Former Marine held in Russia for more than 4 years is back in the U.S.
summary: Former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman released from jail in Russia
story: A former U.S. Marine who spent more than four years in a Russian prison and is believed to be seriously ill was back in the United States Tuesday night, a White House official said.
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff said on X that he had the “profound privilege” of welcoming Robert Gilman, 32, home. He praised President Donald Trump for his release.
“He can now finally return to his family and receive the medical care he needs,” Witkoff said.
Trump earlier announced the release on Truth Social, saying Gilman was freed after he discussed the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said Gilman, a teacher, was released “very much on a Humanitarian Basis,” with no exchange of prisoners having taken place. He was expected to land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C.
The president added in his post that he had spoken to Gilman “and he had one request — A GREAT cheeseburger when he lands. I will take care of that!”
The Russian government has not commented on the release.

About 50 days ago, Gilman was diagnosed with a “dissociative stupor — a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat,” Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., said in a statement following the man’s release.

“He was essentially catatonic and also suffered a severe case of pneumonia,” added Markey, who has been campaigning for Gilman’s release. “We don’t yet know the full details of his current condition or the long-term impact on his recovery.”
Gilman’s sister Lexie Hudson thanked Trump in a statement issued by Global Reach, an advocacy group representing his family.
“There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action,” she said.
“I am looking forward to seeing Robert. I haven’t been able to speak with him once since this all began,” she added. “We will make sure that he gets the treatment and support that he needs.”

Before his release, Hudson said in a statement Sunday that she was worried that he would die if he wasn’t freed. “I’m more afraid for my brother than I have been since this horrible nightmare started,” she said in the statement issued by Global Reach.

Her comments Sunday came around a month after Russia’s Kommersant newspaper reported that Gilman had been ​admitted to a hospital. Quoting his lawyer Irina Brazhnikova, the business daily reported that he was receiving treatment but it was too early to talk about a diagnosis.

Gilman, who served in the Marines from August 2019 until August 2020, had been detained in 2022. He was initially handed a 3 ½-year sentence for beating a police officer after being taken off a train for causing a disturbance.

While serving his sentence, Gilman was accused in October 2024 of attacking a prison inspector during a cell check, beating an investigator and assaulting a guard; he was sentenced to eight years and one month.
Last year, his sentence was extended again to 10 years after he was found guilty of assaulting prison guards.
Gilman’s American supporters contend he was ill when he was first arrested and also that he was provoked while in prison into actions that led to further charges.
According to Markey, Gilman was “subjected to physical torture, forced medication, and provocations by Russian authorities” throughout his detention.
“There is no doubt that his treatment by Russian authorities is the reason Robert is in this precarious state today,” he added.
Gilman was one of at least 10 Americans known to be imprisoned in Russia.

title: More than 160 people killed in Colombia’s strongest earthquake in years
summary: At least 132 people were killed Monday in a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that shook western Colombia, collapsing hospitals, schools and other buildings and leaving people trapped under the rubble.
story: At least 169 people were killed Monday in a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that shook western Colombia, collapsing hospitals, schools and other buildings and leaving people trapped under the rubble.

The worst-hit cities include Pereira, Cali, Quibdó, Manizales and Armenia, all of which remain under “red alert,” the nation’s highest-level disaster threat level, according to Colombia’s nonprofit Association of Capital Cities, which provided the death toll.
Seven airports have suspended operations, and hospitals, roads, transportation, aqueducts, energy and telecommunications have been disrupted in the areas hardest hit, it said.
Colombia’s newly inaugurated president, Abelardo De La Espriella, said in a national briefing that 700 people were injured in the temblor and an estimated 5,000 homes were damaged or destroyed.
